Latest completed US session is Thursday 27 Aug close (S&P +0.72% to 7730.99, Nasdaq +1.57%, VIX down to 14.51; per .prices.json). Today's dominant, portfolio-defining event is Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's 22:00 SGT Jackson Hole keynote -- his first as chair -- which is the single highest-volatility catalyst of the week for the levered silver/gold book. 8 of 13 items below are dated 27-28 Aug, well past the 3-5 freshness target, reflecting a genuinely event-dense pre-Jackson-Hole stretch: jobless claims, a Hormuz tanker strike that reverses Wednesday's de-escalation read, gold/silver/oil/crypto price action, and 30-year yields sitting at post-2007 highs. SGX/Singapore-specific news was again the thinnest category; the freshest available item is an Aug 26 bank-dividend/NPL divergence read.

items.headline: Fed Chair Kevin Warsh delivers debut Jackson Hole keynote today -- markets brace for signal on rate path and Fed independence
items.summary: Warsh, who became the 17th Fed Chair in May 2026, gives his first Jackson Hole address at 10:00am ET (22:00 SGT) today, titled 'Financial Innovation: Implications for Payments and Policy.' He has told reporters he'll focus on long-term structural questions rather than near-term guidance, but investors are pressing for clarity after his hands-off communication style this summer helped push the 30-year Treasury yield to its highest since 2007.
items.actionable: This is the single highest-volatility catalyst of the week for the levered silver/gold book -- avoid adding new leverage into the print and be ready for a sharp two-way move in metals and crypto once Warsh speaks.

items.headline: Strait of Hormuz tanker struck, Iran says Oman deal 'not finalized' -- reverses Wednesday's de-escalation narrative
items.summary: UKMTO issued a warning Thursday after an oil tanker was hit by an unknown projectile in the Strait of Hormuz near Oman, even as Iranian FM Araghchi met Qatar's PM in Tehran to discuss reopening the strait. A senior Iranian source told Reuters the Iran-Oman navigational-corridor agreement reported Wednesday has 'not been finalized,' and Trump is reportedly no longer interested in reviving the June memorandum of understanding, adopting harder-line terms.
items.actionable: Wednesday's Iran-Oman de-escalation thesis looks premature -- a tanker strike and stalled talks reinstate the Hormuz risk premium, a reason not to fade the gold/silver safe-haven hedge on de-escalation headlines alone.

items.headline: Jobless claims fall to 203K, below 208K forecast -- layoffs remain low heading into Jackson Hole
items.summary: Initial jobless claims for the week ending Aug 22 came in at 203,000, a decrease of 4,000 from the prior week and below the 208K consensus, though the 4-week moving average ticked up to 205,500. The print confirms the labor market remains resilient even as inflation stays sticky, a data combination the Fed has to weigh in Warsh's Friday speech.
items.actionable: A resilient labor market reduces the odds of an urgent Fed pivot and raises the bar for Warsh to sound dovish today -- a modest headwind for near-term gold/silver momentum absent a dovish surprise.

items.headline: Silver climbs back to ~$69.34, +1.82%, recovering from Wednesday's dip ahead of Jackson Hole
items.summary: Silver rose to $69.34/oz on Aug 27 (spot touching $69.94 intraday), up 1.82% on the day as investors continued weighing the Fed policy outlook ahead of Warsh's speech. This extends August's roughly 18% monthly gain and keeps the metal within its recent multi-week uptrend, still well below January's record of $115.15.
items.actionable: The bounce back toward $69-70 confirms the levered silver position's uptrend remains intact heading into today's Jackson Hole catalyst -- supportive of holding through the event rather than de-risking pre-emptively.

items.headline: Gold slips to ~$4,590-4,600, its biggest one-day % decline in a week, as investors await Warsh
items.summary: Gold's spot price eased to roughly $4,585-4,606/oz on Aug 27, down from Wednesday's ~$4,674 close and marking its sharpest one-day drop in about a week, as traders positioned defensively ahead of Friday's Jackson Hole keynote. December futures opened just under $4,650, down modestly from Wednesday's close.
items.actionable: This looks like a pre-event pause rather than a trend break -- not a signal to trim GDX/miners, but expect the multi-day range to resolve sharply in either direction once Warsh speaks today.

items.headline: 30-year Treasury yield sits near 5.19-5.31%, highest since 2007, as Bessent's bond-buyback relief fades
items.summary: The 30-year yield closed at 5.31% on Aug 17 -- its highest since 2007 -- prompting a Treasury debt-repurchase intervention on Aug 19; by Aug 27 the yield had eased only marginally to about 5.19% as that relief rally fizzled. Analysts frame the persistently elevated long end as setting up an unusually consequential Jackson Hole speech for Warsh.
items.actionable: A long bond market that keeps pushing yields to post-2007 highs despite Treasury intervention signals eroding confidence in fiscal/inflation control -- a structural tailwind for the gold/silver debasement thesis independent of near-term Fed rate moves.

items.headline: Bitcoin near $79,300, Ethereum near multi-week highs -- crypto holds gains into Jackson Hole rather than de-risking
items.summary: Bitcoin opened Aug 27 at $79,027 (+0.6% day-over-day) and traded up to roughly $79,300 by mid-morning ET, its highest opening level since early June, having eased back from Tuesday's $81,235 intraday high. Ethereum likewise opened near its highest level since Aug 22; the rally has been driven by a short squeeze and Treasury-buyback-related risk appetite, with traders now awaiting Warsh's regulatory and rate-path signals.
items.actionable: Crypto holding gains into a high-vol Fed week rather than de-risking suggests positioning still leans bullish, but a hawkish Warsh surprise today is the key downside risk for the BTC position.

items.headline: Core PCE confirmed at 3.3% y/y, GDP confirmed at 1.5% -- in line with consensus, not falling toward target
items.summary: July core PCE rose 0.2% m/m and 3.3% y/y, matching the 0.2%/consensus estimates but still well above the Fed's 2% target; headline PCE ran hotter at 3.7% y/y. Q2 GDP's second estimate held at 1.5% annualized, confirming the consensus figure and keeping the 'sticky inflation, mediocre growth' backdrop intact heading into Jackson Hole.
items.actionable: Confirmed sticky inflation with in-line growth reinforces the case for holding the silver/miners hedge into today's Warsh speech rather than trimming ahead of it.

items.headline: Alibaba's HK$80B AI-infrastructure share placement sparks dilution sell-off, keeps Hang Seng Tech volatile
items.summary: Alibaba fell as much as 8.5% earlier in the week after announcing an HK$80 billion share placement to fund AI-infrastructure capex, dragging the Hang Seng Tech Index down over 2% on Aug 24 alongside Tencent, Meituan, Xiaomi, JD.com and Kuaishou. By Aug 26 the Hang Seng Index had steadied near 25,511 as Alibaba partly recovered, with sentiment also supported by Wednesday's blowout Nvidia print.
items.actionable: The placement funds AI capex that ultimately benefits the broader China-tech AI theme (SMIC, Tencent), but the dilution hit is a reminder that HK tech names funding NVDA-scale buildouts carry real equity-issuance risk -- size the HK tech sleeve for volatility rather than chasing every capex headline.

items.headline: MP Materials trades near $59 as resource sector stays bid amid ongoing China rare-earth export-control overhang
items.summary: MP Materials shares ranged $57.27-$59.86 on Aug 27, part of a broader critical-minerals sector that has 'caught a bid' this month even as China's export curbs on MP and nine other US firms (imposed in June) remain in force. MP has already ceased sales to China and is scaling a Pentagon- and Apple-backed (US$500M) mine-to-magnet supply chain, with Q1 2026 processed-rare-earth revenue nearly quadrupling to $94.4M.
items.actionable: With China's curbs still in force and the reshoring/demand story (defense, EVs, robotics) intact, the rare-earth watchlist thesis remains valid -- a name to monitor for an entry rather than chase after the recent run-up.

items.headline: WTI crude bounces to ~$82.86, +2.5% off Wednesday's low, as Hormuz talks stall
items.summary: WTI crude traded around $82.51-$82.86/bbl on Aug 27, recovering from Wednesday's $80.78 close as reports emerged that the Iran-Oman Hormuz corridor deal was not finalized and a tanker was struck near Oman. This reverses two sessions of declines that had been driven by the initial de-escalation headlines.
items.actionable: No direct energy exposure in the book, but oil's bounce alongside the stalled Hormuz talks reinforces that the inflation/geopolitical-risk angle supporting the silver and gold trade hasn't disappeared just because of Wednesday's premature de-escalation headlines.

items.headline: Singapore banks diverge: DBS and OCBC hit records, OCBC raises dividend 15%, UOB dips on Greater China NPLs
items.summary: Following 2Q 2026 results, DBS and OCBC hit fresh all-time highs with average dividend hikes of 9%, led by OCBC's 15% increase on 22% earnings growth. UOB slipped as investors focused on a rising Greater China non-performing-loan ratio and a cut to full-year fee-income growth guidance.
items.actionable: OCBC/DBS's dividend hikes and record highs support the core SGX bank holdings, but UOB's Greater China NPL uptick is a reminder to watch China-exposure risk within the bank sleeve specifically rather than treating the three banks as a single bloc.

items.headline: Barrick and Newmont settle Nevada Gold Mines dispute for $1.95B; Barrick advances North America IPO
items.summary: Barrick and Newmont resolved their outstanding Nevada Gold Mines joint-venture dispute, with Newmont paying Barrick $1.95B and both companies' Fourmile/Fiberline/Mike projects folded into the JV, the world's largest gold-mining complex. The settlement clears a hurdle for Barrick's planned IPO of its North American gold business by year-end 2026; Newmont separately confirmed 2026 guidance of 5.3M oz and launched a new $6B buyback.
items.actionable: Removal of a longstanding legal overhang plus a confirmed Barrick IPO catalyst is a fundamental (not just gold-price-driven) positive for the GDX/miner sleeve, distinct from the metals-price momentum story.
